fact_text: The government of Pakistan sets the maximum retail price of medicines, so drug makers cannot raise prices on their own; they can only request an increase.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Most active pharmaceutical ingredients and raw materials are imported, so the industry's costs move with the dollar and with international commodity prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Many pharma raw materials are chemicals priced off oil, and in the 2021-2022 commodity supercycle their dollar prices rose two to three times, aided by Chinese plant shutdowns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A sharp rupee devaluation in 2022 and 2023 raised the rupee cost of imported pharma inputs, which is why the industry sought price relief.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the normal annual rule, Pakistan allows medicine price increases of about 7-10% a year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In July 2023 the government allowed essential medicines to rise up to 14% in price, the first relief for the sector that year.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In July 2023 the government allowed non-essential medicines to rise up to 20% in price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In February 2024 the caretaker government approved about 150 hardship cases, letting makers raise prices on medicines whose production cost had risen above the sale price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In April 2024 the government stopped setting prices for non-essential medicines, so companies can set those prices themselves.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A price increase flows largely into profit, so a modest percentage rise in a medicine's price can lift that product's profit by a larger percentage.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Deregulation of non-essential medicines helps most the companies whose revenue share from non-essential products is highest, provided those products face limited competition.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Some medicines already sold below their government ceiling gain nothing from deregulation, since their prices were never capped in practice.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pricing power in pharma comes from brand image and competition; with deregulation, the sector is starting to behave like fast-moving consumer goods, where brands matter more.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A product with little or no close competition has strong pricing power, while crowded markets with alternatives make price increases hard.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst tracks the prices of each pharma company's five to seven main products, which together make up about 60-70% of revenue, on a monthly basis.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's essential medicines list holds about 500 medicines, far broader than in neighbouring countries; the analyst speculates that some could move to non-essential status and be deregulated.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Multinational pharma firms usually get raw materials on credit from their parent companies, while local firms must pay suppliers faster, so cash cycles differ between the two groups.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Local pharma firms focus on generics and bring new technology in with foreign partners, for example by building oncology and biotechnology plants in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Multinational pharma firms grow by bringing established global brands, such as new Panadol variants and Centrum, to the Pakistan market.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's pharma industry is largely a packaging and assembly business: active ingredients are imported and the plants are cheap to build, which the analyst says gives most firms a good return on capital.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes the pharma sector has typically traded at about 15-20 times earnings during bull markets.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'PHARMA SECTOR - Everything you need to know' (YouTube transcript, undated)
